how_it_was_verified: Each probe asserts a KNOWN ANSWER in a fresh interpreter (z3 must return sat for x>3; tree-sitter must parse a function with no error nodes; gcc must compile an ASan binary that then aborts on a deliberate overflow). Importing alone is not accepted, and absence is reported with its own state label.
negative_cases_tested: an importable but broken module -> PRESENT_BUT_BROKEN (a different diagnosis)
an absent non-critical module -> OK, run continues
note_on_runtime_policy: These are BUILD-AND-VERIFY capabilities, not runtime inference. The mission forbids runtime dependence on another model; a SAT solver and a parser are neither. They are declared here so their absence can never be mistaken for a result, which is the failure this file was written for.

rows.name: z3_smt_solver
rows.why: semantic_causal_engine_v1 gates its safety proof on z3 and returns checked=False when it is missing. A caller reading only `safe` cannot tell.

rows.name: tree_sitter_runtime
rows.why: the CPG localiser reports OPEN__NO_CAUSAL_SITES_IN_CPG when it cannot parse, which is the same output a genuinely site-free project produces.

rows.name: tree_sitter_c
rows.why: the C/C++ half of the polyglot CPG silently yields no sites without it.

rows.name: c_compiler_with_sanitizers
rows.why: the memory-safety walls (cJSON) are verified by ASan/UBSan; without a compiler the wall is ungraded, not passed.

the_rule: A run whose output will be quoted must refuse to produce a number when a critical capability is not PRESENT_AND_EXERCISED. The point is not that the dependency is required; it is that its absence must not be reported in the same words as a successful search.
why_this_exists: Measured, twice, in this repository: semantic_causal_engine_v1 returns checked=False without z3 and OPEN__NO_CAUSAL_SITES_IN_CPG without tree-sitter. Both strings are also what a real, successful search can return. A missing dependency was therefore indistinguishable from an honest negative, and a published claim (9/13 blind commits) had no way to reveal which one it was.
